 Judgment

The injured-claimant is before this Court being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 19.12.2017 passed in MVC No.21/2015 by I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT,
Kalaburagi, (for short, 'Tribunal'), seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal by its judgment and award has granted Rs.1,68,000/- as compensation with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization and directed respondent No.1 - owner of the offending vehicle alone to deposit the said compensation along with interest.

The Tribunal has absolved respondent No.2 - Insurance Company from the liability of paying compensation on two counts, namely that, the offending vehicle was plying beyond permissible limit and that the claimant was an unauthorized occupant in the vehicle.

2 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant while arguing the case for enhancement of the compensation submits that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court and this Court, the Insurance Company be directed to pay the compensation at first instance and recover the same from insurer thereafter.

Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company submits that the vehicle in question was registered in the State of Maharashtra and was found to have been met with an accident in the State of Karnataka, therefore, the Tribunal is justified in holding that the vehicle was being plied contrary to the permit conditions.

He further submits that the claimant had come before the Tribunal with unclean hands, as in the first breadth he had claimed to have been traveling along with bullocks and no evidence was led in that regard and in the second breadth he claimed to have been traveling as an unauthorized passenger.
Therefore, he submits that no interference is warranted in the matter and seeks for dismissal of the petition.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
6.
The only ground canvassed in this appeal is with regard to liability of payment of compensation.
It is settled law that plying of vehicle beyond the permit limit cannot be a ground for the Insurance Company not to pay the compensation
. However, as regards the issue of claimant being unauthorized occupant is concerned, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

8. As rightly taken note of by the Tribunal, the claimant in the first instance has pleaded that he was traveling in the offending vehicle along with his bullock, but no evidence in this regard has been produced.
Therefore, he may not be considered as authorized passenger traveling with goods in the offending vehicle.
The reasons assigned by the Tribunal cannot be found fault with.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellawwa and Others - 2020 ACJ 2560, the Insurance Company would be liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and recover the same from the insurer.
